articleTitle: Integrated-Circuit Fabrication Technology
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The papers in this session are excellent examples of the continuing progress in GaAs IC fabrication technology. Two of the papers discuss self-aligned enhancement-depletion process, one with a refractory gate and one with a non-refractory gate. A key issue for all emerging digital processes is threshold voltage control. This topic is addressed in relation to modulation-doped FETs by the third paper. The session closes with the discussion of optimized ion-implantation conditions for analog MMICs.

articleTitle: Packaging
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The packaging of GaAs digital integrated circuits operating at microwave rates and GaAs MMICs operating at frequencies up to and beyond 100 GHz presents extremely challenging materials science and fabrication problems. An invited paper will summarize the current status of high speed/microwave packaging technology, including multilayer ceramic and metal style chip packages and approaches to subsystem packaging. This will be followed by a discussion of a project to develop and test a set of chip carrier encapsulants specifically targeted for GaAs digital integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits I
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The rapid maturation of GaAs integrated circuit efforts is evidenced by current LSI developments and MSI commercial introductions; therefore, it is appropriate to consider the role of GaAs technology in integrated circuits. This session begins with an invited paper comparing high speed GaAs and silicon technologies for digital applications. The session ranges from advanced GaAs E/D FET technology to the demonstration of the largest gate array fabricated to date in GaAs. Rounding out the session are papers which compare the performance of various logic families as well as advanced E/D applications including a 5 × 5 multiplier and a gate array.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: Modeling and Cad for GaAs MMICs
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: In order to realize the benefits of monolithic integration, it is essential that GaAs MMICs be designed to enable insertion into systems with no additional tuning. An accurate circuit simulation before fabrication must includenotonly active and passive device models, but also layout effects. Device models must accurately incorporate large signal nonlinear effects and the effects of temperature variation. In order to be useful, CAD packages must address large scale microwave circuits, interelectrode coupling and dispersion effects. In addition, measurements of circuit and device results and manufacturing line historical parameters must be easily incorporated into design systems that enforce good design methodology.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits III
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session begins by describing advances in MESFET-based digital circuits for data transmission, including multiplexers, demultiplexers and switching matrices, operating (in some cases) up to 2 Gbit/sec. These circuits are implemented in E/D technology, in order to maintain low power operation, or in source-coupled FET-Logic, in order to increase tolerance to FET variations. Subsequently, similar circuits implemented in HBT technology (with higher operating speeds) are presented. The session ends with several papers describing HBT technology developments that advance the state-of-the-art of III-V bipolar devices.

articleTitle: MMIC Amplifiers and Special Purpose Circuits
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs MMICs are rapidly advancing into the millimeter-wave range and are being used in a host of special purpose circuits useful for specific applications. Narrowband power MMIC amplifiers have demonstrated performance up to 44 GHz with power densities in the 0.5 W/mm range. A 15 to 45 GHz small signal MMIC having 6 dB gain across this band will be reported. At lower frequencies an advanced 5 way power combiner has been used to combine 0.5 W MMICs to the 1-2 W power level over a 7-15 GHz bandwidth. Special purpose circuits include a 2.5 to 5.5 GHz, 45 dB gain limiting amplifier, a low-distortion 2-6 GHz push-pull limiting amplifier, a continuously variable L-Band phase shifter, and filter circuits which avoid the use of inductors.

articleTitle: MMIC Applications and Frequency Conversion Circuits
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: MMIC circuits have been developed for a variety of military systems applications. This, as the invited paper that starts this session describes, depends on the availability of production facilities and the cost of MMIC circuits when delivered. The remaining papers describe various MMIC circuits which focus on frequency conversion in mixers. These circuits integrate FET and diode devices into unique configurations that take advantage of monolithic structures at frequencies ranging from 4 GHz to 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Gallium arsenide integrated circuits are extending the performance of a number of signal processing components. This session will illustrate a number of these modules including ADCs, DACs and programmable filters. In addition, a number of components for optical communication systems will be described including drivers, receivers and multiplexers.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits II
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first four papers in this session focus on advances in high speed GaAs static RAMS. Three papers discuss 1 Kbit memories including a 256 × 4 bit CDFL self-timed RAM, a 256 × 4 bit E/D RAM and a 32 × 32 bit AIGaAs E/D implementation. The fourth paper features a very low power 2.5 ns/200 mW 4 Kbit memory fabricated using a self-aligned refractory gate technology.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: GaAs ICs: As Fast as Lightning—and as Unpredictable?
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs ICs have demonstrated impressive high speed performance in a variety of ICs that are critical to commercial and military systems. However, investigation of IC reliability has lagged far behind the search for ultimate performance. As systems groups design GaAs ICs into their systems, the ground rules change. Those who design and fabricate GaAs ICs are asked not only how the circuit performs, but how long and under what conditions that performance can be maintained.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: Digital GaAs-How Do We Break the Ice?
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Suddenly the market projections for digital GaAs have moved out five years. Why? What can be done to change this? What markets will open soon? What aboutsignal processing? This panel will discuss the problems and some solutions for the digital dilemma.

articleTitle: Thermal Management, Radiation Effects, and Electro-Optic Testing
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Four of the papers in this session address IC thermal management. The first paper describes a method for modeling temperature gradients on the chip surface. The next paper gives temperature-dependent models of N- and Ρ channel JFETs, resistors and diodes which allow circuit designers to numerically simulate performance over the full temperature range of -55°C to 125°C. Two papers then discuss circuit approaches for temperature compensation and operation over this temperature range. Two papers address the role of substrate conduction in the presence of pulsed ionizing radiation which can cause signal dropout and/or logic errors. In the final paper of the session, electro-optic techniques are used for contactless probing for signal injection and monitoring.

articleTitle: Materials
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session focuses on the current status of GaAs substrate materials for microwave and IC applications. An invited talk reviews the current technical and commercial status of large-diameter GaAs crystals. Contributed papers on IC-quality 3 inch and 4 inch diameter material, and 10<sup>7</sup> to 10<sup>8</sup> ohm-ern horizontal Bridgman material conclude this session.

articleTitle: Radiation Induced Substrate Currents in a GaAs MMIC Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Measurements indicate that radiation induced currents in GaAs MMIC microstrip circuitry are the principal cause of a transient upset in performance. Currents were observed at both Schottky and Ohmic contacts, while MIM structures remained insulating.

articleTitle: Large Size Dislocation-Free Gallium Arsenide Single Crystals for LSI Applications
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Large size 3 and 4-inch diameter dislocation-free GaAs single crystals with high electrical uniformity were successfully grown by a vertical magnetic-field-applied fully encapsulated Czochralski technique combined with Indoping. It was found experimentally that the crystals grown from As-rich melt with low boron concentration exhibited high activation efficiency of implanted Si.

articleTitle: New Picosecond Optical Techniques for the Control and Measurement of High-Speed GaAs ICs
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We describe several recent experiments that use picosecond optical pulses for the control and measurement of high-speed GaAs ICs. Picosecond optical techniques provide generally superior and powerful alternatives to present measurement techniques used to characterize high-speed ICs. Our work has concentrated on gigahertz digital ICs; however several of the demonstrated techniques and related ideas are also applicable to various analog ICs, including GaAs MMICs. The experiments described include: 1) demonstration of switching of logic states at nodes internal to ICs by optical inputs at appropriate upstream devices; and 2) non-invasive measurement of high-speed on-chip waveforms at various locations within several digital GaAs ICs. Such waveforms were generated on chip either optically or by normal external electrical inputs.

articleTitle: GaAs MESFET 4X4 Crosspoint Switch
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The data rate in digital communications has been increasing and is now entering the GHz region. Efficient digital communication between multichannel systems will require a crosspoint switch with a Gigabit data rate. A 4×4 crosspoint switch for 1 GHz digital communications was designed, fabricated, and tested. The 4×4 crosspoint switch was designed with Source Follower FET Logic, SFFL. SFFL is an Enhancement/Depletion, E/D, FET logic family with delay and power comparable to Direct Coupled FET Logic, DCFL, but with more noise margins. A brief comparison of SFFL and DCFL will be given. A multiplexer design where the crosspoint switch is completely implemented out of logic gates was used. The design considerations such as power, speed, pulse skew, and density will be discussed. The 4×4 crosspoint switch was fabricated using a 1 µm self-aligned WSi<inf>x</inf> gate MESFET process. The 4×4 crosspoint switch chips were tested and completely functional switches were found. The speed of the crosspoint switch was tested with a 1 Gigabit/second pseudorandom nonreturn-to-zero data generator. The output from the 4×4 cross point switch showed error free switching patterns when the 1-Gigabit/second pseudorandom data was the input.

articleTitle: High Yield and Low Power Multiplexer/Demultiplexer by SCFL
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes Multiplexer (MPX) and Demultiplexer (DMPX) composed of Source Coupled FET Logic (SCFL). First, we report the advantage of using SCFL as a basic logic circuit, espesially from the point of view of the allowance for the variation of the FET threshold voltage. The advantage of using double-phase SCFL circuit is demonstrated by circuit simulation. Then its application to MPX and DMPX ICs are reported. The fabricated ICs operate above 1.6 GHz with low dissipation power and high yield.

articleTitle: GaAs/Al0.3Ga0.7As Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors and Integrated Circuits with High Current Gain for Small Device Geometries
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs/Al<inf>0.3</inf>Ga<inf>0.7</inf>As heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) with small emitter geometries have been developed for integrated circuit applications with significantly higher common-emitter DC current gains, $$, than previously reported. Such high current gains are attractive for new digital, analog/digital (A/D) conversion and analog IC design implementations. In this work minimum $$s ≈100-200 and maximum $$s ≈1000-2000 are observed independent of scaling (from single 2×9/5×11 μm<sup>2</sup> emitter to multiple 2×40 μm<sup>2</sup> emitters). These transistors also exhibit unity current gain cutoff frequency, f<inf>T</inf>, up to 24 GHz and have been used to fabricate small-scale integration digital, A/D and analog type circuits operating at up to 4 GHz.

articleTitle: A High-Performance, Low-Temperature Self-Aligned Gate E/D Process
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high-performance, LDD SAGFET E/D process using a substitutional gate, a spacer and arsine over-pressure annealing has been developed. The gate metal is formed at a low temperature after post implantation annealing. Transconductance of 240 mS/mm and K factor of 4.4 mS/mm for 1.4×20 micron E-SAGFET with Vp=+0.1V and a 32 mV std. dev. over a 3" wafer has been demonstrated. An ECL compatible gate array having 561 four-input NOR gates has been developed. Full functionality of 8X8 multiplier, 8-bit MUX and DEMUX, 8-bit adder and divider have all been demonstrated in personalized gate arrays. Fully loaded internal gate delay of 225 ps with 1.5 mW dissipation and 5 ns 8×8 multiplication time have been realized using 1.4 micron gate. Unloaded gate delay of 110 ps was demonstrated with 1.25 micron gate. The E/D technology was based on a conservative, planarized two-level metalization using silicon nitride as an interlayer dielectric. Such ECL compatible E/D gate array products will be made available in the near future.

articleTitle: An Ideal-Profile Implantation Process for GaAs Analog MMICs
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A new implantation process for GaAs analog MMICs is presented. The process is based on the through-oxide-implantation technology which provides an ideal impurity profile with a steep tail for the n layer and a high surface concentration for the n<sup>+</sup> layer. The ideal profile for the active layer has been successfully obtained by optimizing the acceleration voltage and the SiO<inf>2</inf> thickness for through implantation in order to obtain a high surface concentration of the n<sup>+</sup> layer without degradation of the steepness of the n tail. A constituent FET with a 0.3 μm gate-length and a 280 μm gate-width in the X-band amplifier MMICs exhibited an NF value of 1.5dB and an associated power gain of 10.0dB with a DC transconductance of 250mS/mm. This NF value is the lowest one ever attained with the fully implanted GaAs MESFETs.

articleTitle: Development of High Lead Density Mini Chip Carriers for Gallium Arsenide Digital Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Digital Gallium Arsenide integrated circuits are presently being designed as either low lead count devices which operate at GHz rates, or high lead count devices which operate at 25-200 MHz rates; packaging requirements for the two types are somewhat different. We have thus undertaken the development of several styles of chip carriers tuned for the two types of devices. Design criteria and test results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Distributed Monolithic Image Rejection Mixer
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A broadband FET mixer which uses a distributed arrangement of dual gate FETs to provide broadband image rejection has been designed and fabricated in a MMIC format. The circuit demonstrates a novel method of discriminating upper and lower sideband signals without the use of couplers or baluns. The mixer downconverts a 14-20 GHz RF band to a 2-8 GHz IF using a fixed 12 GHz LO. Preliminary results verify the unique image rejection operation of the distributed mixer showing approximately 10-20 dB image rejection, 6 dB conversion loss, 30 dB LO to IF isolation and 20 dB LO to RF isolation throughout the operating band.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Monolithic GaAs Power FET Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Millimeter-wave monolithic GáAs power FETs with total gate widths of up to 400 μm and output powers up to 200 mW have been developed. These amplifiers were fabricated using sub-half-micron gate length FETs on MBE grown epitaxial layers with η + contact layers. A source overlay structure with via groundings has been used for the FET design. Power densities of 0.75 W/mm, 0.5 W/mm, and 0.45 W/mm were obtained at 29 GHz, 34 GHz and 41 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Applicability, Availability and Affordability of GaAs MMICs to Military Systems
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The principal content of this paper is a discussion of the applications of GaAs MMICs to a variety of military systems, wherein high-rate production of large quantities of chips is expected to be required. Examples of these applications include active-element phased arrays, expendable jammers for electronic warfare and millimeter wave sensors for precision-guided munitions. A review of the current availability of GaAs MMICs for projected military applications is also presented. Finally, a discussion of the critical issue of affordability of GaAs MMICs for military applications is presented, including the cost goals which must be met to ensure economic viability. The issues which impact the costs of MMICs, including yield, foundry throughput and the important trade-off between requirements definition and yield, will be discussed. In the context of affordability, a critical concern which must be addressed is the problem of how to ensure quality control at the chip and module levels without overwhelming the established cost goals.

articleTitle: A Single Stage Monolithic Regenerative 1/2 Analog Frequency Divider
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A single stage monolithic regenerative divider operating at 10 GHz has been developed. The divider uses a GaAs FET with parallel feedback to generate the 5 GHz subharmonic output signal in the presence of an input signal. The circuit has an operating bandwidth of 800 MHz at the input signal frequency, and demonstrates a minimum conversion loss of 7.1 dB. The circuit is stable in the absence of an input signal. The chip size is 1.0 mm × 0.65 mm.

articleTitle: A 15 to 45 GHZ Distributed Amplifier using 3 Fets of Varying Periphery
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 15 to 45 GHz GaAs MMIC distributed amplifier is described. The amplifier uses a unique configuration of three FETs of varying periphery. This configuration accommodates more FET periphery than a conventional distributed amplifier, resulting in higher gain and output power. A high yield 0.25 µm gate technology has been developed. A 15-45 GHz amplifier using 0.25 µm gates has been demonstrated. The amplifier is fully monolithic - all bias circuitry and terminations are contained on a .035" × .069" (0.89 mm x 1.75 mm) chip. 5 dB gain has been demonstrated for a single amplifier stage. Two extended bandwidth versions of the 3 FET amplifier of varying periphery were included in the same layout. 2 to 44 GHz and 15 to 50 GHz versions have both been demonstrated with 4 dB gain.

articleTitle: GaAs Monolithic Microwave Active Gyrator
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first realization of an active gyrator in the microwave frequency range is presented. A selective monolithic filter at 0.9 GHz using a resonant circuit with two 0.5 pF capacitors and a gyrator of the transconductance amplifier type has been built on a single GaAs chip. An equivalent Q factor as high as 200 has been obtained.

articleTitle: GaAs Technology for Analog-to-Digital Conversion
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Technologies, circuits, and architectures for GaAs high speed analog-to-digital converters are presented, including consideration of field effect versus bipolar transistors for various AID architectures. Comparisons with silicon bipolar are made for device and circuit performance. The conclusion gives a prognosis for the future of GaAs AOCs.

articleTitle: A 2-6 Ghz GaAs MMIC Limiting Amplifier with Low Second Harmonic Distortion
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 2-6 GHz limiting amplifier using a new push-pull (differential) design has been built. The push-pull design maintained low second harmonic distortion (greater than -25 dBc) when driven 30 dB into saturation. The basic cell used was a four-stage FET limiting amplifier which measured 20 ± 0.75 dB gain and was realized on a 1.2 mm × 2.0 mm chip area.

articleTitle: A GaAs 256 × 4 Static Self-Timed Random Access Memory
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A new GaAs 256 × 4 static self-timed RAM (SSTRAM) with input and output registers and internal write-pulse generation has been designed, fabricated, and tested. Fully functional ECL compatible SSTRAMs have been routinely obtained with equal read and write cycle times of 2.0 ns to 2.3 ns and power levels of 2.5 W to 3.4 W. This provides for a major improvement in memory system performance compared to the present 10 - 12 ns memory system cycle time using 7 ns ECL RAMs. This performance is obtained using GigaBit Logic's proven depletion-mode MESFET technology and innovative circuit design.

articleTitle: High-Speed, High-Accuracy, Self-Calibrating GaAs Mesfet Voltage Coiiparator for A/D Converters
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first GaAs MESFET comparators with internal self calibration circuits are reported. Initial test circuits demonstrated the operation of this self-calibration technique and feasibility of comparator resolutions suitable for correcting most errors in all major subcircuits (including comparators) in 6-10 bit ADC chip ICs at conversion rates up to 2 GHz. Comparator resolutions of one to 5 mV at 1 GHz and yield of about 60% are observed in initial testing.

articleTitle: A 12:1 Multiplexer and Demultiplexer Chip Set for use in a Fiber Optic Communication System
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 1:12 multiplexer and demultiplexer chip set has been developed specifically for use in a fiber optic transmission system. Features not normally associated with 'standard' multiplexers and demultiplexers were included in this pair of parts to ease their integration into the system. The multiplexer features an integral edge triggered register to store the low speed data input, and a high speed clock output that is synchronous with the data output. The demultiplexer features differential inputs for both the high speed clock and data inputs and an integral phase detector whose operation is frequency independent. Both parts are packaged in 44 pin leaded ceramic chip carriers. The pair dissipate 4.5 watts of power.

articleTitle: A High-Speed 1K-Bit High Electron Mobility Transistor Static Ram
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 1-Kbit static RAM with enhancement and depletion-mode devices was designed and fabricated using the high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) technology. The RAM circuit was optimized to achieve ultra-high-speed performance. A subnano-second address access time of 0.6 ns was measured at room temperature for a total power dissipation of 450 mW. The minimum write-enable pulse width required to change the state of memory cell is less than 2 ns on probe testing. The best chip has 3 bits that failed to function, which corresponds to a bit yield of 99.7%. Variations of the threshold voltage inside the memory cell affect its stable functional range. High-speed operation requires more uniform threshold voltage control to achieve fully operational LSI memory circuits.

articleTitle: A High Speed Programmable Transversal Filter
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An integrated transversal filter circuit, fabricated using a simple 1 µm GaAs MESFET technology, is described. The filter uses S60 MESFETs, has two antiphase non-overlapping clocked sample and hold (S/H) delay lines with clock breakthrough cancellation for every S/H cell. On-chip MIM capacitors perform weighting functions to produce three different filter responses, a bandpass and a switchable highpass or lowpass. Operation has been demonstrated using clock frequencies over 1000 MHz.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: GaAs Technology for LSI/VLSI
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: With the advancing maturity of GaAs technology, we are now seeing increasing efforts at the development level and introductory offerings at the commercial level for LSI circuits. A large variety of technological approaches compatible with LSI/VLSI are currently in use or under development. This panel session will first attempt to provide an assessment of the technological trade-offs between various GaAs technologies (i.e., DFET, EFET, HEMT and HBT) in development today. Following this overview, various ion implanted (non-heterojunction) low power depletion-mode and enhancement-mode circuit and fabrication technology options will be discussed. The discussions will focus on specific issues relating to the successful development of these technologies for LSI/VLSI applications.

articleTitle: Lessons of LSI Pilot Production
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The technology developments leading to an LSI GaAs Pilot production capability, demonstrated by fully functional 4K RAMS and 6K gate arrays, have addressed some long-standing technology through the design and fabrication of highly complex, high performance circuits, vital aspects such as GaAs wafer specifications, batch processing techniques, test structure development, design rule and process documentation, package selection, and production screening are rapidly evolving. In this paper, these aspects of GaAs pilot production technology, emanating from research and development in parallel, will be detailed. The critical issues in facility design and equipment selection will first be defined, followed by the attendant pilot production needs for documentation, lot tracking, and yield analysis. The status of GaAs materials will be discussed, along with the type of specifications and problems/solutions observed. Development of a fabrication capability for 20 wafer lots of 3-1n. wafers for the depletion-mode MESFET technology, has resulted in new approaches to lift-off, usage of mix and match lithography, and inspection procedures to enhance yield. The type and results of screening using test monitors will be detailed. The impact of driving for demanding performance and DoD requirements on design rules, package selection and circuit design has placed different, and in some cases, more stringent challenges for GaAs technology than the commercial environment. These differences and impacts on GaAs technology development and pilot production for DoD and the new circuits being developed, e.g., 16K low power, high speed rad-hard RAMs, will be probed.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of GaAs Integrated Circuit Devices
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The GaAs device is modeled as having multiple heat sources on a four-layer structure. By using separation of variable and Fourier expansion technique, analytic solution for the temperature was derived and expressed in terms of double cosine series. A software program was developed to calculate the temperature. The number of terms needed in the double cosine series for the solution to converge was found to be directly related to the ratio of chip size to heat-source size. It was also shown that the CPU time increased drastically with the number of terms. Simulated results of several devices indicate that the thermal resistance can be reduced by more uniform distribution of heat sources on the chip and by using die-bonding material of high thermal conductivity. For device with very small heat source (1.5µm × 20µm), the full-width half-maximum of the temperature distribution on the chip surface is very small (7μm). Accordingly, the peak temperature measured by infrared thermal imaging technique would tend to underestimate the actual value due to the limited spatial resolution.

articleTitle: High Speed and Ultra-Low Power GaAs Mesfet 5×5 Multipliers
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We have fabricated high speed and low power GaAs MESFET 5×5 multipliers using a WSi<inf>X</inf> self-aligned gate enhancement-mode MESFET process. The multiplication time demonstrated by these multipliers is 4.0 nanosecond at a 1 V supply voltage, which corresponds to a gate propagation delay of 133 picosecond with an equivalent fan-out of 2.2 and a power dissipation of 0.13 mW/gate. This result is the fastest speed for multipliers fabricated using ion-implanted MESFET technology and the lowest speed-power product ever for any multiplier circuit implemented using MESFET or AlGaAs/GaAs MODFET devices. The yield of fully funtional multipliers across 3-inch wafers is as high as 72%, which we believe is the highest yield ever achieved in GaAs IC's of this MSI complexity.

articleTitle: Amonolithic Microwave and Digital GaAs Integrated Circuit Chip for L-Band Receiver Applications
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Microwave and digital circuit functions suitable for a global positioning satellite (GPS) and integrated communication, navigation and identification (CNI) avionics system applications have been successfully implemented on a single chip using low-power GaAs enhancement/depletion-mode MESFET technology. GaAs technology, rather than Si, was selected because of its lower inherent noise figure and higher cutoff frequency. Monolithic circuits at L-band in Si with device cutoff frequencies in the range of 4-8 GHz are much more sensitive to process variations than are GaAs monolithic circuits with device cutoff frequencies in the range of 26-30 GHz. Since a GPS receiver receives phase-modulated coded signals at 1575.2 MHz and 1227.6 MHz, and integrated CNI systems at L-band receive signals from 30 MHz to 2000 MHz, GaAs is the appropriate technology choice. Normally, the microwave and digital functions would be implemented on separate chips, requiring a hybrid assembly with its attendant cost, reliability and performance limitations. Integration of the microwave and digital functions using GaAs enhancement/depletion-mode MESFET technology provides the opportunity to avoid these problems, as well as the capability for battery operation for miniature GPS sets, and considerable size reduction in integrated CNI systems. For example, power reduction in the prescalar results in a 2:1 reduction in total receiver power for circuits for a GPS set. A set of microwave, analog (0-2 GHz) and digital circuits were implemented using a single mask set. The monolithic fabrication process was designed to yield manufacturing quantities of digital and microwave circuits on the same wafer. Self-aligned gate MESFETs, implanted resistors, and a range of implantation conditions to tune the monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) and digital circuits independently are features of the process. Self-aligned digital E/D MESFETs with an 0.8 ~m gate length and microwave self-aligned D-MESFETs with an 0.6 ~m gate length were defined by a self-aligned substitutional gate process and optical photolithography. The EMESFETs had a threshold voltage, Vt, tuned by dry recessing to V t = 0.2 V, and digital D-MESFETs toV t = -0.6 Vby direct ion implantation. The mlcrowave D-MESFETs have a V t = 2.5 Vand a drainto-source current of 0.22 mA/~m of gate width at zero gate bias. Lots were run in a pilot production mode with a fabrication cycle of less than five weeks from pattern generation tape to tested dice. The digital dividers were tested to 2.2 GHz and were operated from -55°C to +150°C at 1.7 GHz. Power, excluding the output buffer, was 10 mW at 2 V input. Circuits were operational for a power supply voltage range of 2 Vto 5 V. Circuits were operated from 10 MHz to 2.2 GHz; the lower limit was due to equipment risetimes. The use of enhancement MESFET dividers resulted in a 10:1 power reduction over similar circuits implemented in depletion-mode MESFET technology. The low-noise amplifiers had gain and match characteristics very similar to those amplifiers processed in a standard microwave process; 40 dB at 200 MHz and 25 dB at 1.66 GHz.

articleTitle: VBB Feedback Approach for Achieving ECL Compatibility in GaAs ICs
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An approach is described utilizing a V<inf>BB</inf> logic threshold potential input to feedback circuitry to stabilize all of the logic inputs on an SSI/MSI/LSI GaAs IC chip to ECL compatible levels over temperature and power supply variations.

articleTitle: A GIGA-Bit-Rate GaAs Multi-Functional LSI with Half-Micron Gate Buried P-Layer Saint Fets
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An ultra-high speed GaAs multi-functional LSI is designed using Low-power Source Coupled FET Logic (LSCFL), and is successfully fabricated with 0.5 pi gate Buried p-layer SAINT (BPSAINT). The LSI, including 1202 devices (248 gates), performs 4 or 8 bit multiplexing (MUX), demultiplexing (DMUX), frame pulse generating, and 3-stage synchronous binary counting, which are key functions in various kinds of digital systems. The LSI operates up to 2.5 Gb/s with ECL I/O condition at power dissipation of 1.9 W (including 13 output buffers). Maximum bit-rate reaches 3.0 and 2.8 Gb/s for 4 and 8 bit operations, respectively, by adjusting bias voltages.

articleTitle: A 6K GaAs Gate Array with Fully Functional LSI Personalization
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 6,000 gate array has been successfully designed, fabricated and tested as a demonstration vehicle for DARPA's GaAs Pilot Line Program. The design of the array emphasizes manufacturability and functionality over large variations in process parameters and temperature. Meeting the gate delay goal of about 1nsec is also of prime importance with power dissipation a secondary factor. To demonstrate these goals a 12 × 12 multiplier is personalized on the array. The multiplier and its associated test circuitry consist of more than 19,000 transistors and diodes, thus making it one of the first GaAs large scale integrated circuits. This personalization has been successfully tested and verified and the results correlated to simulation results.

articleTitle: High-Performance Ka-Band GaAs Power Field-Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The Ka-band GaAs power FETs have been optimized. A n + ledge structure device with 0.4 µm long gates was fabricated on MBE grown material. An output power density of 0.75 W/mm has been achieved at 29 GHz with 4.5 dB gain and 17% efficiency. As high as 23% efficiency nas been achieved with power density of 0.6 W/mm. Recent advances in material preparation and device fabrication techniques have pushed the performance of GaAs FETs into the higher frequencies with higher power densities.[1~6] Molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) has received considerable attention as a viable tool for the formation of GaAs epi-layer for power field effect transistors at K-band and above.[4~6] The MBE growth provides very abrupt transition in doping level. The extremely high doped n+ layer (5×10<sup>18</sup>cm<sup>3</sup>) can also be grown. Because of the advantages, we experienced that the power performance of the FETs made on MBE grown material are at least one decibel higher than that of the devices made on VPE or ion implanted material at the operation frequencies above K-band. The material used in this paper was grown using a Perkin-Elmer 425B MBE system configured for 3-inch-substrates. The 3-layer GaAs epitaxial structure consisting of a 1.0 µm undoped buffer layer, a 0.2 µm active layer doped to 3.5×10<sup>17</sup>/cm<sup>3</sup> with Si, and an 0.1 µm n+ contact layer doped to 5×10<sup>18</sup>cm<sup>3</sup> was grown on a 2-inch Cr-doped GaAs (100) semi-insulating substrate (supplied by Comineo). During growth the substrate was held at about 580°C ana was supported bya molybdenum block and retaining ring assembly without indium soldering [7], On the material, n + ledge channel structure devices were made (see Figure 1). It has been shown [8] that devices with this structure have the highest resistance to instantaneous burnout and the highest long-term reliability. We also found that the n + ledge structure significantly improves device power performance over that of conventional devices mainly because of the reduced parasitics.

articleTitle: A 0.1 - 4.5 GHz, 20 mW GaAs Prescaler Operating at 125°C
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We report on the development in the RTC foundry of a new GaAs normally-off presea!er specially designed for high temperature operation. The basic Τ flip-flop is of dual clock master-slave type using composite buffered NOR/OR gates and a complementary clock generator specially designed to extend the low frequency range. Performance measurement for packaged frequency dividers by 2 and 8 indicates a typical operating range of 50 MHz to 4.5 GHz, a maximum operating range of 20 MHz to 6.2 GHz for a sinewave input signal and a typical power consumption of 20 mW and 100 mW respectively. In addition, a typical maximum operating frequency of 4.5 GHz has been achieved at 125°C ambient temperature.

articleTitle: Bulk GaAs Materials Review
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A review is presented of the recent progress made in improving the quality of large-diameter LEC-grown GaAs crystals, in the preparation of ultra-flat, damage-free, wafers and of our current understanding of materials/device interactions which can adversely affect FET performance and yields. In contrast to silicon IC technology, GaAs materials deficiencies present formidable problems for device fabricators. These problems are related to primary defects, i.e., those associated with the GaAs growth process, and secondary defects, i.e., those related to wafer preparation. At present, these remain major obstacles to advancing GaAs IC technology to the point of insertion of GaAs circuits into advanced, cost-affordable, commercial and military systems.

articleTitle: Application of GaAs/(Ga,Al)As Super-Lattices to Dose Rate Hardening of GaAs MESFETs
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: In this paper we report on the first successful reduction, by over two orders of magnitude, of the primary photocurrent due to the substrate conduction in the GaAs MESFET during ionizing radiation. A buffer layer consisting of AlGaAs/GaAs superlattices (30% Al) has been used to provide a series of potential barriers along the path of the generated electron hole pairs travelling between the substrate and the active region. The origin of the persistent current following irradiation has been identified as the modulation of the space charge region at the interface between the substrate and/or buffer layer and the active channel. The persistent current is eliminated when the substrate is grounded.

articleTitle: 2GHz Multiplexer and Demultiplexer using DCFL/SBFL Circuit and the Precise Vth Control Process
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs DCFL 4:1 multiplexer and 1:4 demultiplexer ICs for the operation of 2GHz clock rates were designed and fabricated with high yields. Considering the practical use, small input levels, large output voltage swings, and wide temperature range operations (0 - 75°C) were realized. Power dissipations were as low as 0.39 - 0.74 W. The key technique in the circuit design is the co-use of SBFL circuits with DCFL circuits in order to increase the load drive capability. To obtain high yields, the advanced refractory metal gate self-alignment process and the V<inf>th</inf> adjusting method by the ultra low dose boron ion implantation through the gate metal after the completion of MESFET structure were used.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Semi-Insulating Properties of Undoped GaAs Grown by the Horizontal Bridgman Technique
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Two inch and three inch diameter undoped semi-insulating GaAs has been grown by a modified horizontal Bridgman technique. Due to the reduced thermal gradients used, this method promises more uniform, low EPD material than can be produced by the undoped LEC process. By using pyrolytic boron nitride boats and controlling the growth environment, to reduce background impurities we have overcome the historical problems in producing undoped semi-insulating GaAs by the horizontal Bridgman technique. Van Der Pauw measurements show that this material has resistivities in the 10<sup>7</sup> - 10<sup>8</sup> ohm-cm range. Hall measurements indicate mobilities 4000 cm<sup>2</sup>/V-sec. Preliminary indications are that the dominant level has activation energy of 0.71 eV.

articleTitle: High-Speed MSI Current-Mode Logic Circuits Implemented with Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first medium-scale integrated (MSI) Current-Mode Logic circuits implemented with heterojunction bipolar transistors are reported. MSI circuits consisting of up to 280 HBTs were designed and fabricated. These include an 8-bit universal shift register, a 3-bit register, and a gated full adder. The design considerations, HBT fabrication and device characteristics are described. Proper operation was observed at clock/input frequencies higher than 3 GHz for most of the circuits.

articleTitle: The Fabrication of ENFET, DFET, and Ring Oscillators with Pure Tungsten Gates
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Pure W and WN<inf>X</inf> films have been deposited on GaAs by dc magnetron sputtering. These low stress films can be reliably annealed above 800 °C without peeling. The W films gave more reproducible Schottky diode characteristics with better uniformity while offering lower resistivity (12 µ$$cm) than the WN<inf>X</inf> films (70 μ$$cm). Both enhancement and depletion mode SAG MESFETs have been fabricated using W and WN<inf>x</inf>, with transconductance as high as 240 mS/mm (W gates). Normally off (ENFET) GaAs circuits have been fabricated using pure W SAGFETs that produced ring oscillator gate delays of 25 ps.

articleTitle: Heterojunction Bipolar Dtgital ICs using Mocvd Material
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) with f<inf>T</inf>S of 16.6GHz have been fabricated from GaAlAs-GaAs grown by MOCVD. These devices have been used in ECL divide by four circuits which operate at 2.5GHz. SPICE has accurately modelled these circuits and correctly predicted the failure mode. Simulations show potential for divider operation at 12GHz.

articleTitle: Threshold Voltage Control of Modfet IC
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Threshold voltage (Vth) control has been identified as one of the key issues for achieving higher integration levels of MODFET digital ICs. Our process uses selective reactive ion etching (RIE) of the recesses for both depletion and enhancement gate. We studied and individually optimized three parameters which affect Vth uniformity and reproducibility: 1) MBE growth of the GaAs-GaAl<inf>x</inf>Asi-<inf>x</inf> heterostructure, 2) gate metallization, and 3) RIE conditions. We separated Vth variation due to RIE from Vth variation due to the combination of MBE and gate metallization by processing two types of FETs: 1) depletion-mode FETs (DFETs) formed with gates deposited on the nearly-as-grown MBE surface (no RIE gate recess etch), and 2) enhancement-mode FETs (EFETs) formed with gates deposited in selectively RIE'd gate recesses. For the DFETs, a Vth deviation of 16 mV was achieved across a 2-inch wafer. The median Vth value of each wafer had a 70 mV deviation from wafer to wafer over a four month period. In the case of the EFETs, the best-case deviation of 9 mV was achieved across one quarter of a 2-inch wafer.

articleTitle: High Speed/Microwave Packaging of GaAs Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper summarizes the chip and subsystem packaging problem as related to system integration, reviews the industry's present packaging capability at the chip and subsystem level and reports on developments which are underway by industry packaging leaders. Specific areas addressed include high pin count leadless chip carriers, transistor outline packages, and surface mount devices. Finally, future subsystan integration schemes are evaluated for their low cost and high performance capabilities.

articleTitle: A Monolithic 4 GHZ Image Rejection Frequency Converter
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A complete 4 GHz Image Rejection Frequency Converter has been integrated onto a single GaAs MMIC chip. The chip includes four two-stage RF amplifiers, two three-stage IF amplifiers, an in-phase power divider, a 90° hybrid and two double balanced mixers. The reported circuit downconverts 4 GHz signals directly to a 70 MHz IF signal with 35 dB of RF to IF gain and 13 dB of image rejection.

articleTitle: 30GHz & 60GHz GaAs MMIC Microstrip Mixers
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes the design, fabrication and performance of 30GHz and 60GHz single balanced microstrip diode mixers. The matching networks for these circuits were designed using a mixer analysis program. The measured conversion loss was better than 5.5dB across a 2GHz IF bandwidth at Ka Band and better than 7.7dB over a 4GHz IF bandwidth at V Band. The circuit sizes and the high yield of the processing are consistent with low cost production.

articleTitle: A 2-Watt, 6-18 GHz Power Amplifier Module for EW Applications
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A multi-octave power module was developed for electronic warfare application using broadband monolithic power amplifier chips. The amplifier module demonstrated an output power of 2.2 watts at GHz and a minimum output power of 1.3 watts from 7 to 15.5 GHz.

articleTitle: GaAs Monolithic Limiting Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 2.5 to 5.5 GHz high dynamic range GaAs monolithic limiting amplifier chip has been developed. The chip consists of two parts: diode limiter at the input and a 2-stage feedback linear amplifier at the output. The six-stage limiting amplifier module using these chips has a gain 45 ± 4 dB, limiting output power 12 ± 1 dBm, noise figure < 9 dB, dynamic range > 50 dB, input and output VSWR < 2. The small chip size and circuit simplicity allows the integrated module to be compact and low cost.

articleTitle: 3 GHz, 150 mW, 4 bit GaAs Analogue to Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Using a conventional "flash" structure, a 4 bit GaAs analogue to digital (A/D) converter has been fabricated and measured successfully up to a clock frequency of 3 GHz. This result is the highest speed ever reported for 4 bit ADC's and could lead in the near future to a real break through in performances for future digital signal processing systems. The GaAs chip, fabricated with a N-OFF 1 µm recessed gate process and consuming a mere 150 mW seems to be one order of magnitude more promising than the fastest silicon converters ever reported (5 bit, 500 MHz (1) or 6 bit 200 MHz (2)). Enhancement-mode MESFET's arranged in an original fashion, made it possible to get simple single-clocked comparators, combining a high sensitivity, a large input range and a complete cancellation of low frequency parasitic effects. Moreover, low dislocation density material pulled at LEP, has enabled to reduce the standard deviation of the comparators offset voltage down to 15 mV, and to limit ADC's non-linearities to ± 1/4 LSB (typical).

articleTitle: GaAs IC Family for High Speed Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: For the application to high speed optical communication, we have developed the GaAs IC family: an LED driver IC, trans-impedance amplifier IC's and logic IC's ( shift registers and frequency dividers ). The optical transmitter composed of this LED driver IC has demonstrated 1 Gb/s operation with very small jitters and sufficient on/off ratio ( 13 dB ) of the optical pulses. The combination of this optical transmitter and the receiver, which consists of the trans-impedance amplifier IC and a PIN photodiode, has successfully achieved optical transmission at 500 Mb/s. Furthermore, logic IC's have operated stably over very wide clock frequency range: from lower than 100 Hz to 1.5 GHz ( H bit shift register and 1/8 frequency divider ) or 1.2 GHz ( 8 bit shift register and 1/16 frequency divider).

articleTitle: Continuously Variable L-Band Monolithic Phase Shifters using GaAs
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A phase shift module has been developed that provides 360 degrees of continuous phase shift and over 30 dB of gain control. It consists of two GaAs monolithic circuits. The first circuit is a three-bit fixed bit phase shifter with 45 degree phase steps. The second circuit consists of a variable phase section, which uses variable gain amplifiers in phase differential for a 45 degree variable range, and a variable gain power amplifier.

articleTitle: A High-Speed GaAs 256 × 4-Bit Ram
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A fully functional 256×4-bit GaAs RAM has been demonstrated with an access time of 1 ns and a power dissipation of 700 mW, excluding the final output drivers. A self-aligned-gate E/D MESFET process was used where typical Ε-mode FET's have transconductances of 200 mS/mm. To obtain high yield, a unique Monte Carlo analysis was used to optimize the design.

articleTitle: A 1 Gs/s 8-Bit GaAs DAC with On-Chip Current Sources
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 1Gs/s 8-bit GaAs DAC has been developed which utilizes on-chip current sources to obtain full 8-bit differential linearity. The device includes multiplexed data inputs and an on-chip ECL reference, fully latched data paths, blanking capability, and complementary 50 ohm outputs. DC differential linearity up to 0.025% (consistent with 12 bit resolution) has been observed, and operation has been shown to 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Monolithic Integration of a 3 GHz, MESFET Detector/Preamplifier
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: High performance Interdigitated MSM detectors and photoreceivers have been fabricated using a standard refractory gate, ion-implanted MESFET process which has also been used to fabricate complex digital circuits. A shallow implant under the detector is shown to eliminate the undesirable low frequency gain and large dark currents previously observed in these devices. Bandwidths as high as 3.2 GHz have been observed for a detector-preamplifier combination with detector responsivities as high as 0.45 A/W, and dark currents as low as 5 nanoamps.

articleTitle: A 2.5ns/200mW GaAs 4Kb SRAM
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high speed and low power dissipation GaAs 4Kb SRAM has been developed. In the design, E/D DCFL circuit is adopted. Por high speed addressing and low power dissipation, pre-decorders are applied. To reduce an excess Schottky current, the supply voltage is lowered to somewhat higher than Schottky barrier height. In the fabrication, a WSi<inf>x</inf> self-aligned FET is used for its high performance. To reduce the chip size, a double-level interconnection is adopted. A minimum address access time of 2.5ns has been obtained with the power dissipation of 200mW at Vdd of 0.7V.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of GaAs Logic Families using Universal Shift Registers and Self-Aligned Gate Technology
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A systematic study of four low-power GaAs logic families has been done, comparing the performance of circuits fabricated with advanced refractory self-aligned gate technology. To provide a useful comparison, logic gates, ring oscillators, frequency dividers, and universal shift registers in each logic family were fabricated on the same die. The results show that Direct-Coupled FET Logic (DCFL) is capable of impressive performance and good yields, and is superior to the other three low-power logic approaches studied. A DCFL frequency divider had a maximum toggle frequency of 3.1 GHz and consumed 3.4 mW power, while the DCFL 8-bit shift register worked up to 1.6 GHz and consumed only 58 mW power.

articleTitle: Circuit Performance of Complementary Heterostructure Misfet Inverter using High Mobility 2DEG and 2DHG
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A complementary circuit employing high mobility two-dimensional electron and hole gases(2DEG and 2DHG) induced at the AlGaAs/GaAs heterointerface has been successfully fabricated on an n<sup>+</sup> -Ge/undoped AlGaAs/undoped GaAs heterostructure. Transfer characteristics of a two-stage inverter show sufficiently high and low output levels. A 15-stage ring oscillator shows a minimum delay time of 94 ps at 300 K and 64 ps at 77 K. The circuit simulation using a new gate current model shows that, for mul ti-input logic gate, a NAND gate configuration is superior to a NOR gate configuration, and that a high speed operation below 20 ps at 77 K is possible by reducing the gate length to 0.5µm.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of GaAs Jfet DCFL Integrated Circuits Operating in the Temperature Range of -55°C to 125°C
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The performance of GaAs DCFL circuits are more susceptible to temperature variations because of the smaller logic swings and circuit noise margins compared to silicon circuits. In this work the performance of GaAs JFET DCFL integrated circuits [1] operating over the temperature range of -55° to 125°C is analyzed based on experimental data and circuit simulation to formulate circuit design guidelines needed for operation over the full commercial temperature range.

articleTitle: High Speed Technology Comparison -GaAs VS Si-
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between GaAs and Si high speed technologies. First, the ring oscillator and frequency divider performance of state of the art technology is compared. Next, performance of SRAMs and logic circuits is studied taking into consideration the device size difference and threshold voltage scatter. The prospects of SRAMs and logic circuits using scaled-down devices are also discussed based on circuit simulation.

articleTitle: Macro Evaluation of a GaAs 3000 Gate Array
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 3000 equivalent gate, 64 signal I/O, configurable-cell GaAs array is reported. This enhancement/depletion-mode (E/D) array has been designed to interface with silicon ECL, CMOS, and TTL families. A custom designed, surface mount leaded chip carrier package has been developed with the array. Total array power is about 2.5 Watts plus 20 mW per ECL output driver for this single supply, 160 mil square chip. A special diagnostic circuit personalization is described. This circuit allows a complete assessment of the array logic macro library functional characteristics and the inter-cell fan-in and fan-out circuit loading effects. The diagnostic circuit includes a circuit designed to emulate the silicon 10181 ECL 4-Bit ALU, a popular 10K ECL component.

articleTitle: A Monolithic Microwave and Digital GaAs Integrated Circuit Chip for L-Band Receiver Applications
publicationTitle: 1986 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Microwave and digital circuit functions suitable for a global positioning satellite (GPS) and integrated communication, navigation and identification (CNI) avionics system applications have been successfully implemented on a single chip using low-power GaAs enhancement/depletion-mode MESFET technology. GaAs technology, rather than Si, was selected because of its lower inherent noise figure and higher cutoff frequency. Monolithic circuits at L-band in Si with device cutoff frequencies in the range of 4-8 GHz are much more sensitive to process variations than are GaAs monolithic circuits with device cutoff frequencies in the range of 26-30 GHz. Since a GPS receiver receives phase-modulated coded signals at 1575.2 MHz and 1227.6 MHz, and integrated CNI systems at L-band receive signals from 30 MHz to 2000 MHz, GaAs is the appropriate technology choice.
